rationale: Every q3 filter and the q4 aggregation depend on the same nameable slot in the movie description: its set of genres. Extract a single multi-valued `genres` set once per movie, then each AI.IF("is a <G> movie") compiles to exact set-membership (G IN genres) and q4 compiles to UNNEST(genres) + GROUP BY. One extraction amortizes over all 8 queries.

attributes.name: genres
attributes.description: The set of applicable film genres implied by the title and description, drawn from a fixed controlled vocabulary.
attributes.extract_instruction: Read the title and description and output the set of ALL genres that apply, choosing only from this controlled vocabulary: comedy, sci-fi, horror, thriller, drama, action, romance. Include every genre the plot clearly supports (a film may have several, e.g. a scary supernatural film that is also tense = {horror, thriller}). Do NOT invent genres outside the vocabulary. Emit canonical spellings exactly as listed. If none of the seven apply, output the empty set [].

attributes.name: genre_conf
attributes.description: Per-genre confidence in [0,1], backing the residual fallthrough decision.
attributes.extract_instruction: For each genre placed in `genres`, emit a confidence score in [0,1] reflecting how strongly the description supports it.

predicate_rewrite.q4_aggregate: SELECT genre, COUNT(*) FROM movies t, UNNEST(t.genres) AS genre GROUP BY genre
predicate_rewrite.note: AI.IF(t.title || ' is a <G> movie ...') becomes the constant-time test <G> IN t.genres; the AI.GENERATE genres-array in q4 IS this same extracted set, so no second extraction is needed.

rules: map every surface spelling to a canonical vocabulary term before set insertion
drop any term not in the vocabulary
normalization.note: The controlled vocabulary plus this canonicalization map is the hidden difficulty: without it the model's free-form genre wording (e.g. 'science fiction', 'romantic') would never set-match the query literals ('sci-fi', 'romance'). Built once at compile time so every downstream filter is exact rather than fuzzy.

residual.condition: genres == [] OR max(genre_conf) < theta OR (for a given query G: G absent from genres AND second-best genre_conf for G-adjacent evidence >= theta)
residual.action: For a movie whose extraction is empty or low-confidence, fall through to the original AI.IF(title, description) for only the specific genre G being queried, rather than trusting set-membership.
